claims.statement: Python package dependencies run systemone -> chess, while cli (via the langchain-chess[systemone] extra), apps/server and evals (both listing chess and systemone directly) depend on both chess and systemone; no workspace member depends on cli, server or evals.
libs/chess exposes an optional `systemone` extra that the CLI installs through (`langchain-chess[systemone]`), but langchain_chess source never imports langchain_chess_systemone.

create_chess_agent wraps each user middleware in the write guard, rejects two middlewares declaring the same own state key, and builds the stack ChessCore, then ForcedMoveMiddleware (if forced_move), then guarded extensions, then ChessSummarization when memory=True or a NoSummarization placeholder when fixed_topology=True, and finally StallRetry last, passing it to create_agent with tools=[] and ChessState.
create_chess_agent raises ChessContractError if the compiled graph's input schema exposes keys other than messages and position, or if two middlewares declare the same own state key.

A CallRecorder is attached as a callback to every chess agent graph so provider responses are captured for pricing, the graph is rejected if its input schema exposes keys other than messages and position, and model=None installs a NoModel that raises ChessContractError if called.

build_agent in libs/systemone turns a ChessContext into a chess agent for every surface, calling only the factories a policy needs: llm (chat model, NoSystemOne in System 1's slot under fixed_topology), systemone (no model so memory is off, SystemOneMiddleware with threshold and tournament_threshold forced to 0 and has_model=False) and hybrid (both); surface middleware runs after System 1.

langgraph.json registers the chess graph as apps/server graph.py:make_graph, the FastAPI app from app.py as the HTTP app, auth.py:auth as the auth handler with allow_langsmith_api_keys true, and .env as the env file; the image builds from the uv workspace (source.kind uv, package langchain-chess-server) and dockerfile_lines ADDs the pyproject.toml of libs/chess, libs/systemone, libs/cli and apps/server but not evals.

mise run test runs test:python (pytest -n auto with the 100% coverage gate) and test:web (`vp run -r test`); pytest excludes live and e2e markers by default (`-m not live and not e2e`), which run via mise run test:live (`-m live --no-cov`) and mise run test:e2e (builds the UI first).

mise run dev:web starts langgraph dev (default port 2024) and the web UI (default 5173 under /ui/), refuses to start if either port is in use, points the UI at the server via VITE_API_URL, prints the URLs once both respond, and stops all processes when either exits; ports are overridable with LANGGRAPH_PORT and WEB_PORT.

useGame takes the signed-in Session and runs one useStream on the chess graph with an SDK client built by sessionClient, which adds the session's credentials to every request; a new session yields a new client that reloads the thread. apps/web, apps/review, evals/reports and packages/* form one pnpm workspace whose shared versions live in the catalog.

Server settings treat LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL set but empty as a validation error, whereas a blank OAUTH_CLIENT_ID or ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_ID is treated as unset.

mise run test:uci plays two System 1-only (policy systemone, Jev) lcchess engines with seeds 1 and 2 against each other under fastchess and fails unless both games end with a result and no non-normal/non-adjudication termination (no forfeits).

ServerSettings.typesafe() raises ValueError when TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL is unset and is called only by the server's pooled ranker factory for System 1 models that do not start with the OpenAI Decisions prefix `openai/` (those use LANGSMITH_GATEWAY* credentials); build_agent invokes the ranker factory only for systemone and hybrid policies, so only those policies with a TypeSafe System 1 model need the TypeSafe variables.
build_agent raises ChessContractError when memory is on for a model whose input limit is unknown.

make_graph returns shape() for runless calls (no execution runtime): a graph with no model, NoSystemOne and GameSetupMiddleware that needs no clients or credentials; only runs resolve a ChessContext and call build_graph (build_agent with fixed_topology=True, GameSetupMiddleware and a pooled ranker using a fresh ServerSettings), and both paths share the same topology.
GameSetupMiddleware writes the run's resolved ChessContext as a client-readable setup key only on the game's first turn, and never again.

Chat model construction lives in langchain_chess.chat_models: chat_model takes a model spec and resolved ModelArguments, checks reasoning effort and that the output limit leaves room in the window, sizes the output budget and sets a profile; the server builds its model with chat_model and the server-surface model arguments, while build_agent's default model uses the local surface.
Memory is a boolean setting (off by default) that keeps earlier turns summarized near the model's input limit; the README states that design decisions and measurements live in the OpenWiki.

ChessContext settings are versioned (currently VERSION 3): every schema change bumps VERSION, DEFAULTS freezes each version's keys and defaults, MIGRATIONS carry one version to the next (version 2 to 3 retires SemIf models in favor of Jev), migrate rejects unknown keys (or drops them) and newer versions, and resolve merges migrated sources over the defaults with later sources winning and an explicit null resetting a key.
The server resolves a run's settings from assistant context first and then config configurable, treating a source without a version as the current version and dropping keys the settings don't have.

mise run generate:settings runs langchain_chess_server.codegen to write ChessContext's JSON Schemas and TypeScript into packages/chess-ui/src/generated, and a test fails when the committed generated files are stale.

The evals workspace member (langchain-chess-evals, binary lcchess-evals) is never published and nothing imports it; mise tasks eval:positions:build, eval:positions:upload, eval:systemone and eval:systemone:baseline drive it, and it is included in the pytest, coverage, ruff and ty configuration.

StallRetry is always the last middleware in the core stack and retries only the provider call, once and without delay, on stream-stall errors (langchain-openai's StreamChunkTimeoutError); other errors still fail the turn and a stalled attempt records no call.

The CLI's uci and play commands build a ChessContext from an optional --config settings file (load_file) overlaid with their flags, and their agent factories call the shared build_agent with that context and a checkpointer.
System 1 is either a TypeSafe classifier (default `typesafe/jev-latest`, Jev) or, for models prefixed `openai/`, OpenAI Decisions; the ranker picks the client by that prefix.

Calls are priced locally: genai-prices for LLM and TypeSafe calls, a local per-token rate for OpenAI Decisions System 1 calls; a call with no known price or approximated usage is incomplete, and a turn's cost is complete only if every call is priced and complete.

The web app's Root renders App only for a signed-in Session (none, apiKey sent as x-api-key, or oauth sending a freshly fetched Bearer access token per request), and admits a session after checkAccess POSTs /assistants/search, treating 401/403 as missing or refused sign-in and a fetch failure as unreachable; Root's signIn, check and storage are injectable for tests.

The server auth handler verifies Bearer tokens as EdDSA JWTs issued by LangSmith (issuer and audience https://api.smith.langchain.com) and admits only tokens whose client_id and organization_id match OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and ALLOWED_ORGANIZATION_ID; unset settings refuse every token, invalid or expired tokens get 401 and mismatched ones 403, while API keys bypass it via allow_langsmith_api_keys.

The web build reads VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, VITE_LANGSMITH_ORGANIZATION_ID and optional VITE_LANGSMITH_SSO_SLUG; without a client id only API-key sign-in is offered, and a client id without an organization id makes Root show a misconfigured-build error.
